title: Task and timer counts per seeded case, and the timer offsets beyond the FSD P3 AC-ALT-P3-011 offsets, are not in the sources
source: RWB-E1-065 sections 4 and 11; FSD P3 A2.11 to A2.13 and AC-ALT-P3-011; Temporal and Drools slide 4; RWB-P1-E1065-CON
description: The legacy sandbox story fixes the case volumes, the seed, the exception shapes and the boundary accounts, and the module FSD fixes the service level offsets of one worked case (warning on day 7, breach on day 8, escalation to RW-TEAMMGR under R-UNI-30) and the prescription timer (warning 6 months before the legal deadline). Neither source states how many tasks and timers a seeded case carries beyond that, whether an expired timer is seeded as expired, or the offsets of the other timer rows, so the story seeds one open task and one active timer per active case and treats both counts as parameters.
evidence: RWB-E1-065 section 4 steps 6, 7 and 8 seed cases, shapes and access rows only and name no task or timer; section 11 lists no task or timer field range; FSD P3 A2.11 sets the clock from the timer table and AC-ALT-P3-011 gives one worked SLA case; the Temporal slide 4 gives the prescription warning of one worked case.
owner_role: TechX and the P3 business analyst
proposed: Fix one open task and one active timer per active case in the seed, and set the remaining timer offsets as rows of the timer table at load review; no code, criterion or value changes if the counts differ.

title: The distribution of the 2,812 seeded cases across the 12 queues and 48 members is not in the sources
source: RWB-E1-065 BR4, BR5 and section 4; FSD P3 AC-P3-006-01, A2.7 to A2.10; Temporal and Drools slide 4
description: The legacy story fixes the case volumes and the number of cases per exception shape, and the module FSD fixes the 12 queues and 48 member rows with capacity 40 and the overflow queue, but no source states how many of the 2,812 cases sit in each queue or with each member, nor how the exception shapes are spread over the queues. The story therefore distributes the cases by product group to the queue rows of the seed file and keeps every member inside the cap of 40 open cases.
evidence: RWB-E1-065 BR5 gives 1,226 Mortgage, 1,296 Hire purchase and 290 SSME; FSD P3 AC-P3-006-01 gives 12 queues and 48 member rows; AC-ALT-P3-006-02 gives capacity 40 and overflow queue TDR-BKK-OVF; no source gives a per-queue case count.
owner_role: TechX and the P3 business analyst
proposed: Distribute the cases by product group to the queue rows of the seed file and cap every member at 40 open cases; adjust the distribution as a seed-file row when the allocation rules are tuned.

title: The rwb-case login name, the DEV read-only role name and the field identifiers of six seeded tables are not in the sources
source: RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 10, 11 and 13; Architecture v5 slide 20; Template and Rules R4, R5.5 DP-02 and DP-15
description: The legacy story names the DEV database role rwb_sandbox_read and one recovery login, and Architecture v5 fixes one login per service without naming it. Legacy section 11 lists field ranges for the case, account, party, deviation, document, interaction and reference tables only, so the field identifiers of queue, queue_member, assignment, task, timer, case_entry_exclusion and reference_version are not stated in any source read for this work package. The story keeps the legacy read-only role name, uses the rwb-case login as DP-02 states it, and takes the missing field identifiers from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary at implementation.
evidence: RWB-E1-065 section 13 grants SELECT to role rwb_sandbox_read; section 11 lists DF-CAS, DF-INT, DF-DOC, DF-EXT and DF-REF ranges and no queue, assignment, task or timer range; Architecture v5 slide 20 states one login and one schema per service without a name.
owner_role: TechX and the ACE DB team
proposed: Keep rwb_sandbox_read for the DEV read role and set the rwb-case login at the platform schema story RWB-PLT-NF06-DB; confirm the field identifiers against the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 before the migration is cut.

title: The decision code and the payload of the decision records the seed writes are not in the sources
source: RWB-E1-065 section 11; FSD P3 A2.1 and A2.5; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON
description: Legacy section 11 says decision_log_entry and interaction receive their rows from running the Workbench jobs against the sandbox, and names no decision code, actor or payload for a seeded entry. The case creation and exclusion stories name the rules they apply and the version (AC-P3-001-01 with EXCL-2026.11) but not the decision code of the record. The story writes one local decision record per seeded exclusion and one for the worked case and uses the code of the case story that owns the action.
evidence: RWB-E1-065 section 11 lists no decision record field and no decision code; FSD P3 AC-ALT-P3-001-01 names the exclusion reason, the rule ID and the version only; the decision-record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON fixes the envelope and not the code.
owner_role: TechX and the rwb-decision contract owner
proposed: Use the decision code of RWB-P3-E1018-APP for the seeded creation and the code of RWB-P3-E1019-APP or the exclusion rule for a seeded exclusion, and confirm both at the decision-record contract review; the seed and its criteria do not change if the codes differ.
